newsitem.title: UK: Shipping losses up in first quarter - insurance body.
newsitem.headline: Shipping losses up in first quarter - insurance body.

text.p: The tonnage of ships lost in the first quarter of 1997 more than doubled to 295,547 gross tons, although the number of ships lost was only one higher at 32.
"It is impossible to discern a trend from first quarter figures. But the doubling in tonnage lost is a disturbing factor," the Institute of London Underwriting (ILU) said in a statement.
The tonnage lost in the first quarter of 1996 was initially reported as 144,237. This figure has since risen to 210,953 and the number of ships lost to 39 from 31.
The ILU said that tonnage and ship losses for the first quarter of this year would also rise as casualties are confirmed and some partial losses are deemed to be total constructive losses.
The ILU represents companies operating in the London marine and aviation insurance markets.
Notable losses in the first quarter included -
-- The 86,595 gt tanker Tpao, insured value $10 million.
-- The 8,633 gt containership Vikartindur, insured value 24.4 marks.
-- The 44,875 gt tanker Chestnut Hill, insured value $13 million.
-- The 13,157 gt tanker Nakhodka, insured value $1.8 million, but large pollution claims likely.
Five tankers, three bulkers and three containerships were among the vessels lost in the three months to end March. Most of the ships lost were built in the late 1960s and early 1970s.
Deaths from marine incidents reported by the ILU fell to 45 from 78, but the Institute noted that its statistics refer only to vessels over 500 gross tons.
The latest figures for the total number of ships lost last year are 113 with a tonnage of 700,848, compared with 112 and 760,512 in 1995.
